'''Péter Pulay''' (born September 20, 1941) is a [[Theoretical chemistry|theoretical chemist]]. He is the Roger B. Bost [[Distinguished professor|Distinguished Professor]] of Chemistry in the Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry at the [[University of Arkansas]], [[United States]].<ref name=mp>{{Cite journal |date=2007-10-10 |title=Péter Pulay, man and scientist |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/00268970701584089 |journal=Molecular Physics |language=en |volume=105 |issue=19-22 |pages=2439–2445 |doi=10.1080/00268970701584089 |issn=0026-8976}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Peter Pulay |url=https://iaqms.org/members/pulay.php |website=International Academy of Quantum Molecular Science}}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Pulay was born in [[Veszprém]] in the [[Kingdom of Hungary (1920–1946)|Kingdom of Hungary]]. He attended [[Eötvös Loránd University]] and graduated with a diploma in chemistry in 1963. He then studied at [[University of Stuttgart]], where he received a PhD in theoretical chemistry in 1970. His supervisors were [[Josef Goubeau]] and Heinzwerner Preuss. After graduation, Pulay worked at the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]] after graduation and was promoted to [[Docent|docent]] at [[Eötvös Loránd University]] in 1977. Since 1982, he has been professor at [[University of Arkansas]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=BIOGRAPHICAL DATA Peter Pulay |url=https://pulay.hosted.uark.edu/vita.htm |website=pulay.hosted.uark.edu}}</ref><ref name=mp></reF>

One of his most important contributions is the introduction of the gradient method in [[quantum chemistry]]. This allows the prediction of the geometric structure of a molecule using [[Computational chemistry|computational chemical]] programs to be almost routine. He is the main author of the [[PQS (chemical)|PQS]] [[computational chemistry]] program.

His work was cited in the official background material for the 1998 [[Nobel Prize in Chemistry|Nobel Prize in chemistry]].

== Honors and awards ==
Among many honors, he was made a Foreign Member of the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]] in 1993. He is a member of the [[International Academy of Quantum Molecular Science]]. In 2017, Pulay received the ACS Award in Theoretical Chemistry.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wang |first=Linda |date=2025-01-21 |title=ACS Award in Theoretical Chemistry: Peter Pulay |url=https://cen.acs.org/articles/95/i1/ACS-Award-Theoretical-Chemistry-Peter.html |website=Chemical & Engineering News |language=en}}</ref>
